correctness.rationale: For each orbit a_k=||T^kx||^p and tail sum S_k, absolute Cesàro boundedness applied to T^kx with remaining horizon n-k+1 yields S_k <=K(n-k+1)a_k. Therefore S_{k+1}/S_k <=1-1/[K(n-k+1)] for k<n, without dividing by vanishing orbit norms; combine k=0 and iterate through n-1. The weighted backward shift on ℓp with w1^p=2K-1 and w_j^p=1+(K-1)/(Kj) for j>=2 has nonincreasing positive weights. For e_j the cumulative orbit norm A_j obeys A_1=2K and A_j=1+w_j^pA_{j-1}=K(j+1). Every partial average is <=K because the nonzero orbit norms increase with k and later terms vanish; coordinate additivity extends this to arbitrary ℓp vectors. e1 gives optimal K and e_n attains the power product for all n. Gamma identity and K=1 endpoint checked. The result is a complete infinite proof; finite recurrences are supplementary.
residual_risks: Universal only for bounded operators and p>=1, K>=1, integer horizons; no extremizer uniqueness, stability, or q-Cesàro transfer assertion.
